# Rotary Cutter Unit for Agricultural Mower

## Overview

A rotary cutter unit for an agricultural mower comprises a housing incorporating a rotary bearing, together with a rotor assembly that is supported by this bearing for rotation about a defined axis relative to the housing. This arrangement forms the fundamental structural basis for the cutting mechanism, enabling controlled rotational movement while maintaining the necessary support and alignment during operation.

## Rotor Assembly Configuration

The rotor assembly is centered around a shaft that extends along the rotational axis and features two functionally distinct ends. At one end, the shaft incorporates a drive input element, which is configured to receive rotary drive from an external power source, such as a power take-off (PTO) shaft or gearbox arrangement typical of agricultural mowing equipment. At the opposite end, the shaft includes a drive output element, whose purpose is to transmit the received rotary motion onward—typically to a cutting blade, disc, or other working component responsible for performing the mowing function.

## Frangible Element for Overload Protection

Positioned between the drive input element and the drive output element is a frangible element, which is formed as a deliberately weakened portion of the shaft. This weakened section is engineered to fail—breaking under conditions of excessive load—thereby interrupting the transmission of drive from the input side to the output side of the shaft. This feature serves as a critical safety and protective mechanism: in the event that the rotor assembly encounters an obstruction, foreign object, or other cause of sudden torque spike (such as striking a rock or other solid debris during field operation), the frangible element is designed to fail in a controlled and predictable manner. This controlled failure protects more expensive or difficult-to-replace components—such as the gearbox, drive shaft, or power source—from experiencing damage due to shock loading or torque overload.

## Retention Mechanism

While the frangible element is essential for protecting the drivetrain from overload damage, its failure creates a potential secondary issue: once the shaft breaks, the drive output element and its associated components (such as the cutting blade) could become separated from the housing entirely, posing a safety hazard due to uncontrolled detachment of a rotating mass.

To address this concern, the rotor assembly incorporates a retention mechanism specifically designed to prevent the drive output element from separating from the housing in the event that the frangible element breaks. Importantly, this retention mechanism is configured such that it does not impede the continued rotational freedom of the drive output element relative to the housing—even after the frangible element has failed. This allows the output element (and any attached blade or cutting tool) to continue rotating freely, without drive input, until it naturally decelerates and comes to rest, rather than being suddenly restrained in a manner that could cause further mechanical damage or hazard.

### Retention Element Detail

The retention mechanism achieves this dual functionality—axial retention combined with continued rotational freedom—through the inclusion of a radially extending retention element. This retention element is positioned between the drive output element and the housing, situated such that it restricts relative axial movement between these two components. By constraining axial displacement while permitting rotational movement, the retention element ensures that even after the frangible element breaks and drive transmission ceases, the drive output element (along with any cutting components attached to it) remains securely coupled to the housing structure. This prevents the output element from being ejected or falling away from the mower unit, thereby maintaining a safer overall system in the event of a shaft failure, while still allowing the disconnected output side to rotate freely and dissipate residual kinetic energy in a controlled fashion.

## Summary

Taken together, this rotary cutter unit design provides an effective combination of overload protection—via the frangible element—and post-failure safety retention—via the radially extending retention element. This ensures that, in the event of an overload causing the frangible element to break, the agricultural mower's cutting components remain safely attached to the housing, minimizing the risk of component ejection while still allowing for free rotation until the rotor assembly comes to a natural stop.

# Rotary Cutter Unit with Frangible Shaft Protection for Agricultural Mowers

## Background and Field of Invention

Agricultural rotary mowers are subjected to significant operational stresses during field use, particularly when cutting blades encounter obstacles such as rocks, tree stumps, wire fencing, or other debris hidden within vegetation. These impact events can generate sudden, extreme torque loads that, if transmitted unchecked through the drive train, may cause catastrophic damage to expensive components such as gearboxes, drive shafts, and power take-off (PTO) mechanisms. To address this persistent challenge in agricultural equipment design, rotary cutter units have been developed that incorporate deliberate mechanical safeguards to protect the broader drive system from damage.

## Detailed Description of the Rotor Assembly

The rotary cutter unit disclosed herein comprises a rotor assembly housed within a protective housing, the assembly being centered around a rotatable shaft that serves as the primary conduit for transmitting rotary drive from an input source—typically connected to a tractor's power take-off—to an output element responsible for driving the cutting blades or discs.

A critical feature of this shaft is the incorporation of a frangible element, which constitutes an intentionally weakened section positioned along the length of the shaft between the drive input element and the drive output element. This frangible portion may be formed through various manufacturing techniques, including a reduced cross-sectional diameter, a machined groove or notch, a change in material composition, or a combination of these approaches, all calculated to create a predetermined breaking point with a specific, calibrated failure threshold.

During normal operating conditions, the frangible element performs no distinguishing function beyond its role as an integral part of the shaft, seamlessly transmitting torque from the input to the output without impediment. However, should the rotor assembly encounter an obstruction or experience a sudden torque spike exceeding the frangible element's designed tolerance, this weakened section is engineered to fracture before damage propagates to more critical and costly components of the mower's drive system. Once fractured, the frangible element effectively severs the mechanical connection between the drive input and drive output elements, immediately halting the transmission of rotary motion to the cutting mechanism.

## Retention Mechanism for Post-Failure Safety

While the frangible element's primary function is to protect the drive train through controlled failure, a significant engineering challenge arises immediately after such a breakage occurs: without additional safeguards, the drive output element—now mechanically disconnected from the input—could potentially separate entirely from the housing. Such separation would pose serious safety risks, including the possibility of the output element and any attached cutting components becoming projectiles, or the loss of an integral part of the mower unit during operation.

To mitigate this risk, the rotary cutter unit incorporates a dedicated retention mechanism designed to work in concert with the frangible element. This retention mechanism features a retention element that extends radially—that is, outward from the central axis of the shaft—positioned strategically to engage with a corresponding feature on the housing or an adjacent structural component. The radial orientation of this retention element is specifically configured to prevent axial displacement of the drive output element, effectively acting as a physical stop or constraint that keeps the output element captured within the housing assembly.

Critically, the design of this retention element ensures that while the drive output element is restrained from separating axially, it remains free to rotate about its own axis even after the frangible element has broken. This distinction is essential: the retention mechanism does not attempt to lock the output element in a fixed rotational position, which could itself create hazards or complicate the diagnosis and repair process. Instead, the output element may continue to spin freely—whether due to residual momentum, contact with the ground or vegetation, or other incidental forces—without transmitting drive to it, and without risk of it flying loose from the unit.

## Advantages and Practical Implications

This combination of a frangible shaft element and a complementary radial retention mechanism provides several notable benefits for agricultural mower operators and equipment manufacturers alike:

1. **Drive Train Protection**: By providing a sacrificial, low-cost component designed to fail before more expensive drive train elements are compromised, the overall repair costs associated with obstacle strikes are substantially reduced.

2. **Enhanced Operator Safety**: The retention mechanism ensures that even after a breakage event, no components are ejected from the housing, thereby protecting operators, bystanders, and nearby equipment from potential injury or damage.

3. **Simplified Maintenance**: Because the frangible element is typically designed as a replaceable or serviceable component, repair following a breakage event can often be accomplished quickly and economically, minimizing equipment downtime during critical harvesting or mowing seasons.

4. **Continued Mechanical Integrity**: The ability of the output element to rotate freely post-failure, rather than becoming rigidly seized, reduces the likelihood of secondary damage that might otherwise occur if the broken components were to bind or jam within the housing.

## Conclusion

The rotary cutter unit described represents an integrated approach to managing the inevitable mechanical stresses encountered in agricultural mowing operations. By combining a purpose-built frangible shaft section with a thoughtfully engineered radial retention mechanism, this design achieves the dual objectives of protecting valuable drive train components from catastrophic failure while simultaneously safeguarding against the hazards associated with component separation, thereby enhancing both the durability and safety profile of the overall mowing implement.

# The Word "The"

"The" is the most commonly used word in the English language, appearing in written and spoken communication far more frequently than any other word. Despite—or perhaps because of—its simplicity, "the" plays an essential grammatical role as the definite article, distinguishing specific, known entities from general or unspecified ones.

## Grammatical Function

Unlike "a" or "an," which introduce something new or unspecified (indefinite articles), "the" signals that the speaker and listener share an understanding of what is being referenced. For example:

- "I saw **a** dog" suggests any dog, previously unmentioned.
- "I saw **the** dog" implies a specific dog already known to both parties, perhaps mentioned earlier in conversation.

This distinction, though subtle, is fundamental to clear communication and is one of the more challenging aspects of English for non-native speakers, particularly those whose languages lack articles altogether, such as Russian, Japanese, or Mandarin Chinese.

## Historical Origins

"The" derives from Old English demonstrative pronouns, particularly "þē" and "sēo," which were part of a more complex system of grammatical gender and case. Over centuries, English simplified its grammar, and these various forms merged into the single, invariant word "the" that exists today, unburdened by gender or number agreement—unlike its counterparts in many other European languages (e.g., "le/la" in French or "der/die/das" in German).

## The Word's Ubiquity

Linguistic studies consistently rank "the" as the most frequent word in English corpora, accounting for roughly 5-7% of all words in typical texts. Its prevalence stems from its universal applicability: it can precede virtually any noun, singular or plural, concrete or abstract, without alteration.

## A Word of Deceptive Simplicity

Though small and seemingly mundane, "the" carries significant weight in shaping meaning. Its presence or absence can alter emphasis, implication, and even legal interpretation in formal documents. Philosophers and linguists have examined how such a minor word encodes complex ideas about specificity, shared knowledge, and definiteness—proving that even the humblest components of language can hold profound significance.

In essence, "the" exemplifies how the smallest linguistic units often perform the heaviest communicative lifting, silently structuring our understanding of the world one sentence at a time.

# Rotary Cutter Unit with Frangible Shaft Element and Overload Retention Mechanism

**[0001]** In accordance with one embodiment, a rotary cutter unit for an agricultural mower comprises a housing, a rotary cutting element rotatably supported relative to the housing, and a drive shaft assembly operatively coupling a power input source to the rotary cutting element for imparting rotational motion thereto. The drive shaft assembly includes a drive output element configured to engage a rotatable spindle or hub associated with the rotary cutting element, and a frangible shaft element interposed in a torque-transmitting path between the power input source and the drive output element. The frangible shaft element is configured with a predetermined cross-sectional geometry, material composition, and/or localized stress-concentration feature, such as an annular groove, reduced-diameter neck portion, or perforated web, such that the frangible shaft element is structurally configured to fracture at a predetermined torque threshold or impact load exceeding normal operating conditions, thereby protecting downstream and upstream drivetrain components from damage attributable to encountering a foreign object, rock, stump, or other obstruction during a mowing operation. In further accordance with this embodiment, the rotary cutter unit includes a retention mechanism operatively associated with the drive output element and the housing, the retention mechanism being configured to maintain mechanical engagement between the drive output element and the housing following fracture of the frangible shaft element, such that the drive output element is prevented from separating from the housing and being ejected therefrom during continued rotation of the rotary cutting element or upon subsequent operator handling. In one aspect, the retention mechanism comprises a retaining collar, tether member, capture flange, or bearing assembly disposed about at least a portion of the drive output element, the retention mechanism being dimensioned and configured to permit relative rotational and/or limited axial movement of the drive output element relative to the housing while substantially preventing complete separation therebetween. It will be appreciated that by retaining the drive output element within or upon the housing following a shear event, the rotary cutter unit reduces the likelihood of component loss, secondary damage to adjacent machine structures, or hazard to nearby personnel, while simultaneously enabling rapid identification and replacement of the frangible shaft element to restore the rotary cutter unit to an operative condition.

# Patent Claim Summary: Agricultural Mower Rotor Assembly with Breakaway Shaft Protection

## Technical Field

This disclosure relates to agricultural mowing equipment, and more particularly to a rotor assembly incorporating a driveshaft with an integrated overload protection mechanism that prevents catastrophic damage to the cutting mechanism and drivetrain components upon impact with foreign objects, while maintaining structural retention within the housing.

## Summary of Claimed Invention

**Claim 1** (Independent): An agricultural mower rotor assembly comprising:

a housing defining an internal cavity;

a rotor shaft rotatably supported within the housing, the rotor shaft comprising:
- a drive input end configured to receive rotational torque from a power source;
- a drive output end operably coupled to a cutting element;
- an intermediate weakened section disposed axially between the drive input end and the drive output end, the weakened section defined by a reduced cross-sectional area relative to adjacent shaft portions, the reduced cross-sectional area configured to fracture at a predetermined torque threshold lower than a torque threshold of the drive input end, the drive output end, and the housing, thereby preventing damage to the housing and drivetrain upon rotor impact with a foreign object;

a radial retention feature disposed on the rotor shaft, positioned to engage a corresponding retention structure formed in or coupled to the housing, the radial retention feature configured to maintain axial positioning of at least a portion of the rotor shaft within the housing subsequent to fracture of the weakened section, thereby preventing separation and ejection of shaft fragments from the housing during continued operation or deceleration of the mower.

**Claim 2** (Dependent on Claim 1): The rotor assembly of Claim 1, wherein the weakened section comprises a reduced-diameter neck portion, an annular groove, a cross-drilled bore, or a combination thereof, forming a stress concentration zone engineered to yield in shear or torsion prior to yielding of adjacent shaft segments.

**Claim 3** (Dependent on Claim 1): The rotor assembly of Claim 1, wherein the radial retention feature comprises a flange, shoulder, retaining ring, or radially-extending collar integrally formed with or affixed to the rotor shaft, the radial retention feature having an outer diameter exceeding an inner diameter of a bearing bore or bushing aperture formed in the housing, such that the radial retention feature is captured against axial withdrawal through the housing aperture.

**Claim 4** (Dependent on Claim 1): The rotor assembly of Claim 1, wherein the radial retention feature is positioned on a side of the weakened section corresponding to the drive output end, such that upon fracture, the drive output end and cutting element remain radially retained and rotatably supported within the housing, preventing separation of the cutting element from the mower deck.

**Claim 5** (Dependent on Claim 1): The rotor assembly of Claim 1, further comprising a bearing assembly disposed within the housing and configured to rotatably support the rotor shaft on at least one side of the weakened section, wherein the radial retention feature is positioned proximate the bearing assembly to maintain radial and axial alignment following fracture.

**Claim 6** (Dependent on Claim 1): The rotor assembly of Claim 1, wherein the weakened section is configured to fracture in response to torque generated by rotor impact with an obstruction, without complete severance of the rotor shaft into disconnected fragments, the weakened section instead permitting limited relative rotational displacement between the drive input end and the drive output end.

**Claim 7** (Independent — Method Claim): A method of protecting an agricultural mower drivetrain, comprising:

transmitting rotational torque through a rotor shaft from a drive input to a cutting element via a drive output, the rotor shaft extending through a housing;

upon the cutting element encountering an obstruction generating torque exceeding a predetermined threshold, fracturing an intermediate weakened section of the rotor shaft disposed between the drive input and the drive output, the weakened section configured with a reduced cross-section to fracture prior to damage occurring in the housing, drive input, or drive output;

retaining, via a radial retention feature disposed on the rotor shaft, at least a portion of the fractured rotor shaft within the housing to prevent axial ejection of shaft fragments during continued rotation or deceleration of the mower.

## Additional Claim Directions (for prosecution flexibility)

- **Material/manufacturing claims**: specifying the weakened section formed via machining, casting, or additive manufacturing with a stress-riser geometry calculated using known fracture mechanics principles.
- **Multi-piece shaft claims**: covering embodiments where the drive input and drive output are separate shaft segments joined by a shear pin, shear bolt, or frangible coupling insert, with the radial retention feature disposed on the housing-facing surface of one or both segments.
- **Serviceability claims**: directed to a rotor assembly configured for field-replacement of the fractured shaft segment without full disassembly of the housing, utilizing the radial retention feature as a removable/reinstallable interface.
- **Safety claims**: directed to prevention of high-velocity ejection of shaft or blade fragments as a safety mechanism, referencing operator protection standards.

---

*Note: This summary is a drafting aid illustrating claim structure and scope for the described mechanical concept. Actual patentability requires a formal prior art search, novelty/non-obviousness analysis, and review by a registered patent practitioner to ensure compliance with 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, and 112 requirements.*

# CUTTER UNIT ASSEMBLY FOR ROTARY MOWING APPARATUS

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to agricultural and turf maintenance equipment, and more particularly to a cutter unit assembly for rotary mowing apparatus incorporating a frangible safety element configured to shear upon application of excessive torque or impact loading, while further comprising a retention mechanism operative to maintain rotational coupling and prevent complete separation of components following shear failure.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Rotary mowing apparatus, including but not limited to disc mowers, drum mowers, and flail-type cutting units, commonly employ a plurality of cutter units mounted upon a rotating cutter bar or similar support structure. Each cutter unit is typically driven via a shaft assembly operatively coupled to a power source, such that rotational energy is transmitted to a cutting element for severing vegetative material.

During operation, cutter units may encounter foreign objects, obstructions, or other impact events that impart substantial torque or shock loading to the drive train. In the absence of a suitable overload protection mechanism, such loading may propagate through the drive system, potentially causing damage to the power source, gearbox, drive shaft, or other associated components. It is known in the art to incorporate a frangible or sacrificial element within the drive train, configured to fail under predetermined loading conditions, thereby isolating the remainder of the drive system from damage.

However, a disadvantage associated with conventional frangible safety elements arises upon shear failure thereof: absent a suitable retention mechanism, the cutter unit, or a portion thereof, may become completely detached from the cutter bar or support structure, presenting a hazard to nearby personnel and equipment, and further necessitating retrieval and reassembly of the separated components prior to resumption of mowing operations.

Accordingly, there exists a need in the art for a cutter unit assembly incorporating a frangible safety element which, upon shear failure, permits continued rotation of the cutter unit while positively preventing complete detachment thereof from the cutter bar or support structure.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with one aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a cutter unit assembly for rotary mowing apparatus, comprising:

a housing configured for mounting upon a cutter bar or analogous support structure of the mowing apparatus;

a rotary bearing disposed at least partially within the housing, the rotary bearing configured to rotatably support a shaft assembly relative to the housing;

a shaft extending through, or in operative association with, the rotary bearing, the shaft comprising a drive input element disposed at a first end thereof and configured for operative coupling to a power source, and a drive output element disposed at a second end thereof, opposite the first end, and configured for operative coupling to a cutting element;

a frangible safety element interposed within a torque-transmitting path between the drive input element and the drive output element, the frangible safety element being configured to shear upon application of torque exceeding a predetermined threshold value, thereby interrupting transmission of rotational torque between the drive input element and the drive output element; and

a retention mechanism configured to maintain operative association between the shaft and the housing, or between respective portions of the shaft, following shear failure of the frangible safety element, such that the drive output element remains rotatable relative to the housing while being restrained against axial or radial displacement sufficient to effect complete separation from the housing.

In accordance with a further aspect, the retention mechanism comprises a retaining member disposed in encircling relation to at least a portion of the shaft, the retaining member being dimensioned so as to engage a retention feature formed upon or affixed to the shaft, such that, upon shear failure of the frangible safety element, the retention feature abuts the retaining member, thereby preventing axial withdrawal of the shaft from the housing while permitting continued rotation thereof.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF EXEMPLARY EMBODIMENTS

### General Configuration

Referring now to exemplary embodiments of the present disclosure, a cutter unit assembly, generally designated by reference numeral **10**, is provided for use with a rotary mowing apparatus. The cutter unit assembly **10** comprises a housing **12** configured for fixed or removable attachment to a cutter bar (not shown) of the mowing apparatus, such attachment being effected by way of fasteners, welding, or other suitable means as will be apparent to persons skilled in the art.

The housing **12** defines an internal bore or cavity **14** configured to receive a rotary bearing **16** therein. The rotary bearing **16** may comprise a rolling-element bearing, such as a ball bearing or roller bearing assembly, or alternatively a bushing or plain bearing configured to permit rotational movement of a shaft **18** relative to the housing **12** while constraining radial movement thereof.

### Shaft Assembly

The shaft **18** extends axially through the rotary bearing **16** and comprises a first end **20** and a second end **22**, opposite the first end **20**. The first end **20** is configured to define, or to operatively receive, a drive input element **24**, which may comprise a splined coupling, a keyed shaft portion, a universal joint yoke, or other torque-transmitting interface configured for operative connection to a power take-off shaft or other drive source of the mowing apparatus.

The second end **22** of the shaft **18** is configured to define, or to operatively receive, a drive output element **26**, which may comprise a mounting flange, hub, or analogous structure configured for affixation of a cutting element, such as a rotary blade, disc, or knife assembly (not shown), thereto.

### Frangible Safety Element

Interposed within the torque-transmitting path defined between the drive input element **24** and the drive output element **26** is a frangible safety element **28**. In certain embodiments, the frangible safety element **28** may comprise a shear pin extending transversely through the shaft **18** and engaging a coupling member disposed thereabout. In alternative embodiments, the frangible safety element **28** may be integrally formed as a reduced-diameter or necked-down portion of the shaft **18** itself, configured to fail preferentially at a predetermined torque threshold.

The frangible safety element **28** is dimensioned and configured such that, under normal operating conditions, torque is transmitted substantially without loss from the drive input element **24** to the drive output element **26**. Upon occurrence of an overload event—whether arising from impact with a foreign object, jamming of the cutting element, or other abnormal loading condition—the frangible safety element **28** is configured to shear or fracture, thereby interrupting the torque-transmitting path and preventing further transmission of torque to the drive output element **26**.

### Retention Mechanism

In accordance with the present disclosure, the cutter unit assembly **10** further comprises a retention mechanism **30** configured to maintain the shaft **18**, or a portion thereof comprising the drive output element **26**, in operative association with the housing **12** notwithstanding shear failure of the frangible safety element **28**.

In one exemplary embodiment, the retention mechanism **30** comprises a retaining ring, circlip, or analogous annular member **32** disposed within a corresponding groove **34** formed in an internal surface of the housing **12** or within a bore of the rotary bearing **16**. The shaft **18** further defines a shoulder, flange, or enlarged-diameter portion **36** positioned such that, upon shear failure of the frangible safety element **28** and consequent axial or rotational displacement of a portion of the shaft **18**, the shoulder **36** engages the annular member **32** in an abutting relationship, thereby preventing further axial displacement of the shaft **18** sufficient to effect withdrawal thereof from the housing **12**.

Notably, the retention mechanism **30** is configured such that engagement between the shoulder **36** and the annular member **32** does not impede rotational movement of the shaft **18** relative to the housing **12**. Accordingly, following shear failure of the frangible safety element **28**, the drive output element **26** and any cutting element affixed thereto remain capable of rotation—whether driven by residual momentum, incidental contact, or otherwise—while being positively restrained against separation from the housing **12**.

In alternative embodiments, the retention mechanism **30** may comprise a cable, chain, or flexible tether extending between the drive output element **26**, or a portion of the shaft **18** associated therewith, and the housing **12** or a fixed portion of the cutter bar, such tether being configured with sufficient slack to permit normal rotational operation while preventing complete separation upon shear failure of the frangible safety element **28**.

In yet further embodiments, the retention mechanism **30** may comprise interengaging formations disposed upon respective portions of the shaft **18** disposed to either side of the frangible safety element **28**, such formations being configured to maintain rotational and axial engagement therebetween independent of the structural integrity of the frangible safety element **28**, whereby torque transmission is interrupted upon shear failure while mechanical continuity of the shaft **18** is nonetheless preserved.

### Advantages

It will be appreciated by persons skilled in the art that the cutter unit assembly **10** as hereinabove described provides significant advantages over conventional arrangements, including without limitation: (i) protection of upstream drive train components from damage resulting from overload conditions, by virtue of the frangible safety element **28**; and (ii) prevention of hazardous detachment of the cutter unit, or portions thereof, from the mowing apparatus following such overload events, by virtue of the retention mechanism **30**, thereby enhancing operational safety and facilitating convenient post-failure servicing and replacement of the frangible safety element **28**.

## CLAIMS (EXEMPLARY)

**1.** A cutter unit assembly for rotary mowing apparatus, comprising:
a housing configured for mounting to a support structure of the mowing apparatus;
a rotary bearing disposed within the housing;
a shaft rotatably supported by the rotary bearing, the shaft comprising a drive input element and a drive output element;

# Engineering Disclosure: Sacrificial Shear Point Drive Shaft Assembly

## Field of the Invention

The present disclosure relates to power transmission components for rotary mower implements, and more particularly to a drive shaft assembly incorporating a designed sacrificial weak point that protects upstream drivetrain components, gearboxes, and prime movers from damage resulting from sudden overload conditions, while simultaneously retaining the fractured output element within the housing to prevent loss of the component and reduce the risk of secondary damage or personal injury.

## Background

Rotary mower cutting assemblies are frequently subjected to impact loads arising from contact with foreign objects, rocks, stumps, or compacted debris. Such loads, if transmitted directly through the drive train, can result in catastrophic failure of gearbox internals, spindle bearings, or the prime mover output shaft—components that are substantially more costly and labor-intensive to replace than a dedicated shear element. It is therefore advantageous to engineer a specific, predictable failure location into the drive shaft itself, such that overload energy is dissipated through controlled fracture of a sacrificial section rather than propagating damage to adjacent, higher-value components.

## Summary of the Disclosure

Disclosed herein is a drive shaft component for a rotary mower assembly comprising an input portion configured for coupling to a power source, an output portion configured for driving a cutting element, and an intermediate sacrificial section disposed therebetween. The sacrificial section defines a reduced cross-sectional area, a machined groove, a material transition, or a similarly engineered stress concentration feature calibrated to fail at a torque threshold below the damage tolerance of upstream drivetrain components, yet above the torque range experienced during normal operating conditions.

Upon the drive shaft experiencing a torque load exceeding the calibrated threshold—such as would occur upon sudden impact of the cutting element with a fixed or semi-fixed obstruction—the sacrificial section is configured to fracture in a controlled and predictable manner, thereby mechanically decoupling the output portion from the input portion and arresting further torque transmission to the prime mover and associated gear reduction components.

Importantly, the assembly further comprises a retaining element disposed about or adjacent to the sacrificial section and configured to maintain the fractured output element in substantial positional alignment within the housing following failure. The retaining element may take the form of a surrounding sleeve, a captive pin, a tethering strap, a shoulder feature formed integrally with the housing, or a combination thereof, such that upon fracture, the severed output portion—together with any attached cutting element or coupling hardware—remains contained within the housing envelope rather than being ejected or permitted to fall free. This containment function reduces the risk of secondary impact damage to surrounding components, minimizes the potential for the detached element to become a projectile hazard to nearby personnel, and facilitates straightforward retrieval and replacement of the failed component during subsequent maintenance.

## Advantages

The disclosed configuration provides a cost-effective, field-serviceable overload protection strategy that (i) localizes wear and failure to an inexpensive, replaceable component; (ii) preserves the operational integrity of the gearbox, spindle, and prime mover during overload events; and (iii) enhances operator and bystander safety by preventing uncontrolled ejection of the fractured drive element from the housing.

# ROTOR ASSEMBLY FOR AGRICULTURAL MOWER CUTTING UNIT

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to agricultural cutting machinery, and more particularly to a rotor assembly for a mower cutting unit incorporating bearing support structures, an overload protection mechanism employing a frangible shaft section, and a retention arrangement for constraining axial displacement of a rotating output element while permitting substantially unimpeded rotational movement thereof.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Rotary mower cutting units typically employ one or more rotors driven at high rotational speeds to effect cutting of crop material such as hay, grass, or similar vegetation. During operation, cutting elements mounted upon such rotors may encounter foreign objects, rocks, or other obstructions within the field, generating impact loads and torque spikes substantially exceeding normal operating conditions. Absent suitable overload protection, such events may propagate damaging forces into the drivetrain, gearbox, or power take-off (PTO) system of the associated implement, resulting in costly repairs and extended equipment downtime.

Additionally, rotor assemblies of this type require robust bearing support to accommodate both radial loads arising from cutting operations and axial loads arising from vibration, gyroscopic effects, and irregular terrain contact. A need exists for a rotor assembly that integrates reliable bearing support, sacrificial overload protection, and secure yet low-friction axial retention of the output element in a compact, serviceable configuration.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with the present disclosure, there is provided a rotor assembly for a farm mower cutting unit comprising a rotor housing, an input shaft rotatably supported therein by upper and lower bearing assemblies, an output shaft coupled to the input shaft through an intermediate frangible shaft section configured to fracture upon experiencing torque loads exceeding a predetermined threshold, and a retention structure disposed proximate a lower end of the output shaft for restraining axial displacement thereof while permitting substantially free rotational movement. The rotor assembly further comprises a cutting element mounting flange affixed to the output shaft for supporting one or more cutting blades or knives.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENT

### 1. General Arrangement

Referring generally to the rotor assembly (10) of the present disclosure, the assembly comprises a rotor housing (12) defining an internal cavity (14) configured to receive and support a rotatable shaft arrangement extending along a longitudinal rotor axis (A-A). The rotor housing (12) is adapted for mounting to a cutterbar or deck structure (not shown) of an agricultural mower via a mounting flange (16) formed integrally with or affixed to an upper portion of the housing (12).

The shaft arrangement comprises an input shaft (20) extending downwardly from an upper drive coupling (22), through the internal cavity (14), to a frangible coupling region (30), below which extends an output shaft (40) terminating at a cutting element mounting flange (50).

### 2. Upper Drive Coupling and Bearing Support Structure

The upper drive coupling (22) is configured to receive rotational input from a gearbox, drive shaft, or belt-driven pulley arrangement associated with the mower's power transmission system. The upper drive coupling (22) is affixed to, or formed integrally with, an upper end of the input shaft (20).

The input shaft (20) is rotatably journaled within the rotor housing (12) by means of a bearing support arrangement comprising at least an upper bearing assembly (24) and a lower bearing assembly (26), axially spaced apart along the rotor axis (A-A). In the preferred embodiment, each of the upper and lower bearing assemblies (24, 26) comprises a sealed ball bearing or tapered roller bearing unit having an inner race press-fitted or otherwise secured upon the input shaft (20), and an outer race secured within a corresponding bearing bore (28) formed within the rotor housing (12).

The upper and lower bearing assemblies (24, 26) cooperate to react both radial loads generated during cutting operation and residual axial (thrust) loads transmitted through the input shaft (20), thereby maintaining precise rotational alignment of the input shaft (20) relative to the rotor housing (12) and minimizing deflection under operational loading. A bearing spacer sleeve (29) may optionally be disposed intermediate the upper and lower bearing assemblies (24, 26) to maintain a predetermined axial preload and to prevent inadvertent axial creep of the bearing inner races along the input shaft (20).

Seal members (25), such as lip seals or labyrinth seal arrangements, are preferably disposed adjacent the upper and lower bearing assemblies (24, 26) to inhibit ingress of dirt, moisture, and crop debris into the internal cavity (14), thereby preserving bearing longevity.

### 3. Frangible Shaft Section for Overload Protection

Disposed intermediate the input shaft (20) and the output shaft (40) is a frangible shaft section (30), also referred to herein as a "shear section" or "breakable coupling region." The frangible shaft section (30) is preferably formed as a reduced-diameter, necked-down portion of an otherwise continuous shaft member, or alternatively as a discrete coupling pin or shear pin element (32) interconnecting the lower end of the input shaft (20) with the upper end of the output shaft (40).

In one preferred embodiment, the frangible shaft section (30) comprises a machined annular groove (34) formed circumferentially about the shaft, defining a reduced cross-sectional area calculated to yield a predetermined torque threshold at which the material will fracture in shear or in a combined shear-and-bending mode. The cross-sectional geometry, groove radius, and material selection of the frangible shaft section (30) are selected such that, under normal cutting loads, the section exhibits sufficient strength to transmit driving torque without deformation, while under an overload event—such as contact between the cutting element and a fixed obstruction—the section will fracture cleanly, thereby mechanically decoupling the output shaft (40) from the input shaft (20) and preventing propagation of damaging torque and impact loads rearward into the drivetrain, gearbox, and PTO components.

In an alternative embodiment, the frangible shaft section (30) may comprise a replaceable shear pin (32) disposed transversely through mating bores formed in overlapping end portions of the input shaft (20) and output shaft (40), such that upon overload, the shear pin (32) fractures, permitting relative rotational slippage or disengagement between the input and output shafts (20, 40). A protective collar (36) may surround the shear pin (32) to retain fractured pin fragments and facilitate ease of replacement during field service.

It will be appreciated that the frangible shaft section (30) is preferably configured as a readily replaceable, low-cost, sacrificial component, such that following an overload event, a service technician may readily access and replace the fractured section without requiring disassembly of the bearing support structure or the cutting element mounting flange (50).

### 4. Output Shaft and Cutting Element Mounting Flange

The output shaft (40) extends downwardly from the frangible shaft section (30) through a lower bore (42) formed in the rotor housing (12), terminating at a cutting element mounting flange (50) disposed exterior to the housing (12). The mounting flange (50) is configured to receive and secure one or more cutting blades, knives, or flail elements (not shown) via fasteners engaging a plurality of mounting apertures (52) formed circumferentially about the flange (50).

### 5. Retention Structure for Axial Restraint of the Output Shaft

In accordance with a further aspect of the present disclosure, the rotor assembly (10) further comprises a retention structure (60) disposed proximate the lower bore (42) of the rotor housing (12), configured to restrain axial displacement of the output shaft (40) relative to the housing (12) while permitting substantially unimpeded rotational movement thereof about the rotor axis (A-A).

In the preferred embodiment, the retention structure (60) comprises a retaining ring or snap ring (62) seated within an annular retention groove (64) formed circumferentially about the output shaft (40), the retaining ring (62) being configured to abut a corresponding shoulder or thrust bearing surface (66) formed within the lower bore (42) of the rotor housing (12). In this configuration, upward or downward axial displacement of the output shaft (40) relative to the housing (12) is resisted by engagement between the retaining ring (62) and the thrust surface (66), while the output shaft (40) remains free to rotate relative to the retaining ring (62) and housing (12).

In an alternative embodiment, the retention structure (60) comprises a thrust washer (68) or low-friction bushing element disposed intermediate the retaining ring (62) and the thrust surface (66), configured to reduce frictional resistance during relative rotation between the output shaft (40) and the stationary housing structure, thereby minimizing parasitic power loss and heat generation during sustained operation.

In yet a further embodiment, the retention structure (60) may comprise a lower bearing race integrated with the lower bearing assembly (26), configured with an axially-facing shoulder engaging a corresponding retaining collar (70) fixed to the output shaft (40) via a set screw, press fit, or splined engagement, such that axial loads imparted upon the output shaft (40)—for example, due to impact of the cutting element with the ground or an obstruction—are transmitted through the retaining collar (70) into the lower bearing assembly (26) and thence into the rotor housing (12), without impeding free rotational movement of the output shaft (40).

The retention structure (60) thereby cooperates with the upper and lower bearing assemblies (24, 26) to maintain the output shaft (40) in stable axial position relative to the rotor housing (12) throughout the operative life of the assembly, notwithstanding axial loading events encountered during field operation, while preserving low-friction rotational characteristics necessary for efficient power transmission.

### 6. Operation

In use, rotational power is supplied to the upper drive coupling (22), driving the input shaft (20) via the upper and lower bearing assemblies (24, 26). Under normal operating conditions, torque is transmitted through the frangible shaft section (30) to the output shaft (40), driving rotation of the cutting element mounting flange (50) and associated cutting elements. Axial loads generated during operation are reacted by the retention structure (60) in cooperation with the bearing assemblies (24, 26), maintaining the output shaft (40) in stable axial position while permitting free rotation.

In the event that a cutting element encounters an obstruction generating a torque load exceeding the predetermined threshold of the frangible shaft section (30), the section (30) will fracture, mechanically isolating the output shaft (40) from continued driven rotation by the input shaft (20), thereby protecting upstream drivetrain components from damage. Following such an event, the frangible shaft section (30) may be readily accessed and replaced via disassembly of the rotor housing (12), without necessitating replacement of the bearing assemblies (24, 26) or the retention structure (60).

---

a frangible shaft section disposed intermediate said input shaft and said output shaft, said frangible shaft section configured to fracture upon experiencing a torque load exceeding a predetermined threshold, thereby mechanically decoupling said output shaft from said input shaft; and
a retention structure disposed to restrain axial displacement of said output shaft relative to said rotor housing while permitting rotational movement of said output shaft relative
